short: A highly innovative and devastating Russian offensive that shattered the Austro-Hungarian army and forced Germany to redirect forces.
full:
On 4 June 1916, General Aleksei Brusilov launched a massive Russian offensive across a wide front in Volhynia and Galicia. Discarding conventional tactics of narrow, prolonged bombardments, Brusilov used short, accurate artillery barrages and specialized shock troops to exploit weak points simultaneously across the line. The Austro-Hungarian defenses collapsed completely, and the Russians advanced over forty miles in a matter of days.

The offensive was a spectacular tactical success and the greatest Russian victory of the war, capturing hundreds of thousands of prisoners. It forced Germany to halt its attack at Verdun and transfer significant forces to the East, effectively breaking the Austro-Hungarian army as an independent fighting force. However, the staggering Russian casualties further destabilized the empire at home.
